messages:
maya: quick heads-up: babel17b-int4 canary is still noisy. saw 4 OOMs during medium bursts this morning and p95 jumps to ~310ms from baseline ~150ms. compactor activity looks high after ~10m. attaching logs below.

sam: thanks. are we on the recent window change? what are the serving defaults for this canary?

maya: canary config: batch_window_ms=25, batch_max_tokens=4096, max_new_tokens=150, prefetch_stride=2. KV hit looks fine but slot_compactor runs spike memory churn.

oli: pattern sounds like prefetch grabbing KV pages + compactor racing with soft-evict. two levers to try: cap prefetch per-session and tighten soft-evict so we avoid large late allocs. also consider increasing compactor interval if it's thrashing.

maya: paste OOM snippet:
```
[OOM] gpu0 alloc failed 1.1G at token_step 412
model=babel17b_int4
context: active_sessions=12, avg_batch_tokens=160, max_new_tokens=150
free_mem=640MB, kv_cached=4.05GB
slot_compactor: last_run=15s ago, runs_in_1m=4
```

jules: quick hypothesis: large max_new_tokens combined with 25ms window -> occasional microbursts that need big temporary buffers. those buffers plus prefetch allocations push free_mem below threshold and compactor/evict interplay causes fragmentation.

sam: propose a candidate config to test on canary:
```
{"batch_window_ms": 14, "max_new_tokens": 96, "prefetch_cap_per_session": 2048, "kv_soft_evict_threshold": 0.85, "slot_compactor_interval_s": 60}
```

maya: rolled candidate as canary-c2 for 6h. quick numbers after 2h: p50 ~110ms (baseline ~100), p95 ~160ms (was 310), p99 ~480ms (was 820), OOMs=0. compactor runs down to ~0-1/min.

ren: ran a quick synthetic burst load (15rps sustained 10s windows) against canary-c2. observed much fewer allocation failures. GPU utilization unchanged. good signal.

qa: important: lowering max_new_tokens may clip very long generations. ren/qa can run the 200-case regression set (generation-length focused). ren: i kicked the eval, will post diffs.

oli: two follow-ups to watch: (1) prefetch_cap_per_session could delay page fetches for long dialogs and hurt warm-up latency; track session token hist and prefix latency. (2) if compactor interval increases, watch long-term fragmentation growth. may need adaptive compactor that triggers on fragmentation delta instead of fixed interval.

jules: rollout gating suggestion: accept candidate if after 48h A/B (50/50):
- OOM_count reduction >= 50% OR absolute OOM_rate < 0.05%
- p95 latency regression <= +8% and p99 regression <= +12%
- KV_eviction_rate not > 1.5x control
- quality delta on eval set: flagged generations <= 1% regressions (manual review threshold)

sam: I'll schedule a 48h split-run starting tomorrow 08:00 PT. infra-bot can you snapshot and enable OOM + compactor metrics?

infra-bot: snapshot saved snap-1718810800. metrics enabled: babel17b.int4.oom_count, babel17b.int4.compactor_runs_per_min, babel17b.int4.prefetch_cap_hits, babel17b.int4.kv_eviction_rate. Alert rule created for oom_count > 3/hr.

ren: eval finished for 200 prompts: quality regressions flagged 3 prompts (1.5%) where completions truncated vs baseline; average length delta -0.6 tokens. attaching diff summary link: https://redwood-internal/rg/eval/1718811200/diff (private).

qa: 3 flags is slightly above our 1% soft threshold. need human review on those 3. if they are acceptable (formatting/duplicate) we can still proceed with caution. also run a focused long-gen set (50 prompts > 1024 tokens) before promoting.

maya: noted. i'll run the long-gen set during A/B. if the human review says regressions are minor, we can proceed to staggered rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 2h holds.

oli: i'll capture allocator traces if we see any OOMs during A/B. kernel malloc logs + nvml snapshots should help identify fragmentation hotspots.

jules: owners & timeline: sam (run split 48h), maya (metrics + long-gen eval), ren/qa (eval + review), oli (alloc traces), jules (rollout gating). start 08:00 PT tomorrow.

maya: thanks. will post dashboards and links once the run starts. :rocket:
